title: Dyn-Bitpool: A Two-sided Sparse CIM Accelerator Featuring a Balanced Workload Scheme and High CIM Macro Utilization
problem: Current CIM accelerators rarely exploit sparsity in both activations and weights simultaneously. Two-sided sparsity creates unbalanced workload distribution and low hardware substrate utilization in CIM macros.
motivation: Computing-in-memory is energy-efficient, and concurrent exploitation of activation and weight sparsity could further improve performance and utilization.
method: Dyn-Bitpool proposes a CIM accelerator architecture with a balanced workload scheme that manages two-sided sparsity by distributing computation across CIM macros to maintain hardware utilization. The design addresses workload imbalance through dynamic bitpool allocation and improved scheduling.
key_novelty: A balanced workload scheme for CIM that efficiently exploits concurrent activation and weight sparsity while maintaining high macro utilization.
contributions: Two-sided sparse CIM accelerator design with concurrent activation and weight sparsity support
Balanced workload scheme to mitigate workload imbalance from two-sided sparsity
Improved CIM macro utilization through dynamic workload distribution
limitations: Specific performance metrics, energy improvements, and comparison baselines not discussed in abstract.
